entries.title: Kinematics and End Effector
entries.summary: What was discussed. # 3-PRRR Sample Handler: System Flowcharts
entries.body:
# Kinematics and End Effector **Time.** 00:00–00:00, location. ## Discussion What was discussed. # 3-PRRR Sample Handler: System Flowcharts This document describes the full signal and control flow for the single-rail 3-PRRR parallel manipulator and its sample gripper. --- ## 1. Overall System Pipeline From a target coordinate to the realized end-effector position. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["1. Spatial Target Input
Desired end-effector location
Target (X, Y, Z)"] B["2. Kinematic Solver (Raspberry Pi / Host)
Closed-form 3-PRRR inverse kinematics
(X, Y, Z) → (d1, d2, d3)"] C["3. Motion Controller (32-bit MCU firmware)
Displacement to steps: STEPS_PER_MM
Pulse generation + trapezoidal velocity ramping"] D["4. Actuation & Primary Drive Train
3x stepper motors + TMC2209 silent drivers
Continuous GT2 timing belt drive loop"] E["5. Single-Rail Mechanical Transmission (3-PRRR)
3x collinear carriages on central extrusion track
Passive linkage arms with free revolute joints"] F["6. End-Effector Spatial Output
Realized 3D coordinate (X, Y, Z)
Electromechanical parallel-jaw sample gripper"] A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F ``` --- ## 2. Gripper Operation Sequence Full lifecycle of a pick, transit and release. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["1. Pre-Grip & Object Detection
ToF IR sensor (VL53L1X) checks vial presence
Pi commands lead-screw motor to start closing"] B["2. Active Clamping & Lead-Screw Drive
Micro stepper drives parallel jaws inward
Strain gauge load cell flexes under contact force"] C["3. Strain Gauge Signal Conditioning
Wheatstone bridge outputs differential mV signal
HX711 24-bit ADC amplifies and digitizes at 80 Hz"] D{"4. Force Comparison
Is F_meas ≥ F_target?"} E["Continue motor inward drive"] F["Halt motor immediately
Engage holding torque"] G["5. In-Transit Sample Drop Protection
Rail transit begins along Y-axis track
Continuous background strain gauge polling
If F_meas drops below threshold → Drop Alert"] H["6. Sample Release Phase
Target destination reached
Lead-screw motor reverses to retract jaws"] A --> B --> C --> D D -- NO --> E --> C D -- YES --> F --> G --> H ``` --- ## 3. Gripper Force Control Loop The closed loop that clamps the sample at a fixed force and monitors for drops. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["1. Initial Grip Command
Target force threshold set (e.g., F_target = 2.0 N)
Pi commands lead-screw stepper to close jaws"] B["2. Continuous Signal Sampling
Lead-screw closes parallel jaws on sample
HX711 24-bit ADC samples load cell at 80 Hz"] C{"3. Threshold Check
Is F_meas ≥ F_target?"} D["Continue motor inward drive"] E["Halt motor drive instantly
Engage holding current"] F["4. In-Transit Sample Drop Monitor
Rail moves sample along Y-axis track
Background check: if F_meas falls below 0.2 N
→ Alert and halt"] A --> B --> C C -- NO --> D --> B C -- YES --> E --> F ``` --- ## 4. Z-Height Closed-Loop Correction Uses the ToF sensor to correct vertical error against the benchtop. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["1. Real-Time Distance Read
VL53L1X ToF IR sensor measures vertical
height above benchtop: Z_measured"] B["2. Error Calculation
ΔZ = Z_target − Z_measured"] C{"3. Tolerance Check
Does the magnitude of ΔZ
exceed 0.2 mm?"} D["Maintain current trajectory
No adjustment needed"] E["Recalculate 3-PRRR IK
Adjust d1, d2, d3 carriages"] A --> B --> C C -- NO --> D C -- YES --> E ``` --- ## 5. Motion Planning and StallGuard Safety From target coordinate to motion, with jam detection. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["1. Spatial Coordinate Target
Input desired target coordinate
(X, Y, Z) in mm"] B["2. Closed-Form Kinematic Solver
Raspberry Pi computes carriage positions (d1, d2, d3)
using linear 3-PRRR algebraic equations [4]"] C["3. Pulse Generation & Motion
Motion controller converts (d1, d2, d3) to step counts
TMC2209 drivers execute trapezoidal velocity profile"] D["4. StallGuard Safety Back-EMF Loop
TMC2209 continuously monitors motor back-EMF"] E{"Back-EMF spike?"} F["Continue motion"] G["Physical obstacle or jam detected
Emergency interrupt → disable motor torque"] A --> B --> C --> D --> E E -- NO --> F E -- YES --> G ``` ## Decisions Main controller: https://www.pishop.ca/product/raspberry-pi-4-model-b-4gb/ Low level communication: STM32 Nucleo connected with drivers ## Action items - [ ] Kinematic Solver to target step counts — Khushmeet, 2026-11-7

entries.title: SHARE — PDP
entries.body:
# Idea finalization and PDP preparation

## Discussion

### Needs assessment

- Completed a needs assessment for the concept.
- Identified the need for better equipment utilization in self-driving laboratories.
- Drafted the problem statement, objectives, criteria, and constraints.

### Solution concepts

- Outlined our proposal for a bench-mounted sample-handling system.
- Developed several distinct solution morphologies.

### Concept selection

- Defined the design criteria and assigned each a weight.
- Used the weights to build a decision matrix and scored each design in it.
- The monorail tripteron scored highest.

### Timeline

- Set a development timeline.

## Decisions

- The monorail tripteron is our selected design, because it scored highest in the weighted decision matrix.

# Idea name Monorail Tripteron

## Problem
3D Printers are limited in printing long parts such as car pieces. 

## Proposed solution
Create a monorail tripteron system that spans a long y axis.

## Decision notes
N/A

## Objective
- Print parts longer than a desktop printer
- Accuracy on the y-axis
- Affordable
- Easy to calibrate/set up
- Device should be able to fit on a workbench

## Constraints
- Device must use a linear rail
- Device must run on wall power
- Device must not deflect over 1mm
- Device must have an e-stop

## Criteria
- Volume/dimensions
- Accuracy
- Print speed
- Calibration time
- Cost

entries.title: AR Snowboard Goggles
entries.body:
# Idea name AR Snowboard Goggles

## Problem
Snowboarders and skiiers use apps such as Slopes and Strava to track their stats on runs and to locate their friends on other parts of the mountain. However using your phone for these apps poses several problems while on the mountain:
1. drains phone battery quickly
2. unable to check speed while on run
3. need to take off gloves and check phone to use apps

## Proposed solution
Create a goggle attachment that creates a display of speeds and location arrows. The locational arrows point to people in your party and/or mountain structures (chalet, lifts).

## Decision notes
N/A

## Objective
- Display current speed, heading, altitude and direction to nearest friend
- The attachment should be less than $250
- light weight < 500g
- Device should record video footage
- Device should non-invasively attaches to most helmet/goggles
- Device should be water resistant

## Constraints
- Device must operate in sub-zero temperatures
- Device must meet IP44 for snow/water resistance
- Device must not require permanent modifications of goggles or helmet
- Battery must last at least 4 hours
- The refresh rate must be at least 1Hz 
- Device must be usable with winter gloves

## Criteria
- Mass
- Volume/dimensions
- Water/particle resistance
- Battery life
- Refresh rate
- Cost
- Operating temperature

entries.title: Multispectral Search and Rescue Snow Goggles
entries.body:
# Multispectral Search and Rescue Snow Goggles

## Problem
Search and resuce (SAR) workers in harsh environments (i.e. blizzards, snow storms, avalanches) have limited visibility when responding to SOS reports. 

## Proposed solution
Develop a pair of multispectral (i.e. IR, Thermal) goggles which can automatically determine which specturm gives the greatest visibility/contrast. Additionally, goggles can also have HUD which displays location to nearest search party member to assist in search efforts. 

## Why it's worth doing
Since SAR workers will already be wearing snow goggles in extreme environments, a multispectral pair of goggles could enhance successful SAR efforts by giving SAR workers enhanced visibility, especially post-avalanche or during heavy snowstorms for example. 

## Concerns and risks
- Overall package would be too bulky/heavy to be practical
- Refresh rate might not be fast enough and may cause dizzines or motion sickness
- Battery life must last long enough to be useful
- Display resolution must be high enough to allow for small/far away targets to be discernable from wildlife

## Objectives
- Weight should be less 500g
- Battery life should be at least 8 hours 
- Spectral band switching should occur automatically during contrast change
- Refresh rate should be at least 72Hz to mitigate nausea
- Should be able to identify a person within a 3 metre range
- The device should be able to work in cold climates

## Constraints
- Device must operate in sub-zero temperatures
- Device must meet IP44 for snow/water resistance
- Device must not extend further than 10cm beyond a regular goggle profile
- Battery must last 6 hours with continuous use
- The refresh rate must be at least 60Hz 
- Device must be usable with winter gloves

## Criteria
- Mass
- Volume/dimensions
- Water/particle resistance
- Battery life
- Refresh rate
- Visible range
- Cost
- Operating temperature
- Spectral switching time
- Resolution

## Decision Notes
- N/A
